purpose: Acitretin is used to treat severe psoriasis, a skin condition that causes thick, scaly, red patches on the skin. It helps when other treatments have not worked well enough. It may also be used for other serious skin conditions as determined by your doctor.
how_it_works: Acitretin is a strong form of Vitamin A that works by slowing down the growth of skin cells that are multiplying too fast. In psoriasis, skin cells grow way too quickly and pile up, causing those thick scaly patches. This medicine helps normalize that process so your skin can look and feel better.
common_side_effects: Very dry lips, skin, and eyes are the most common side effects — almost everyone experiences this, so keep a good moisturizer and lip balm handy. You may also notice dry mouth, peeling skin on your hands and feet, hair thinning, increased sensitivity to sunlight, headache, or mild joint pain.
warnings: WARNING — This medicine must NEVER be taken during pregnancy or if you plan to become pregnant. It can cause very serious birth defects. Women must use two forms of reliable birth control for at least one month before starting, during treatment, AND for three years after stopping. You must not donate blood during treatment or for three years after stopping. Do not drink alcohol during treatment or for two months after stopping, as it can change the medicine into a form that stays in your body even longer. Regular blood tests to check your liver and cholesterol are required. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen daily.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 25 to 50 mg taken by mouth once daily with the main meal. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how your skin responds and how well you tolerate the medicine. Always take it with food — this helps your body absorb it better and reduces stomach upset.
